title: Marta or Miriam daughter of Baitus
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Marta (or Miriam) daughter of Baitus was also very wealthy. She was present during the siege of Jerusalem before the destruction. Gittin 56a relates that Marta daughter of Baitus, a wealthy Jerusalem woman, sent her servant to buy bread during the siege, but he found none. She went out herself to find food, and animal dung stuck to her foot. According to another account, she found Rabbi Tzadok’s dried figs and became sickened. Before she died she took all her silver and gold and threw it outside, then died. Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai applied to her the verse “The tender and delicate woman among you.” Hyman says that Eichah Rabbah 1:47 recounts the story with many corruptions; see there.

notes.text: The checked Gittin has dung adhering to her foot and spells out Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai. The nausea reading is distinct from a miracle; the source’s Marta/Miriam alternative remains visible.

The consulted Gittin 56a preserves Marta, the successive failed purchases, dung at her foot, the alternative dried-fig account, Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai’s verse and disposal of her wealth. Hyman supplies Marta/Miriam and plural figs; the consulted narrative has a single fig eaten. His “many corruptions” judgment about Eichah Rabbah remains attributed, not an independently completed recension comparison.
